html:
Empress of Russia from 1762 to 1796. Born a minor German princess, Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst, she married the heir to the Russian throne and took power from him.

Her husband became Peter III in 1762 and was unpopular within months. Catherine led a coup with the guards regiments, and he died soon after in their custody. She ruled for thirty four years.

  • She won two wars against the Ottoman Empire and annexed the Crimean Khanate in 1783, giving Russia the north coast of the Black Sea.
  • With Prussia and Austria she carved up Poland and Lithuania in the partitions of 1772, 1793 and 1795.
  • She invited foreign settlers, among them the Volga Germans.
  • She put down the great peasant revolt of Pugachev in 1773 to 1775.

She wrote to Voltaire, bought Diderot's library and collected the paintings that began the Hermitage. Yet the lot of the serfs grew worse under her, as she relied on the nobles. She saw herself as heir to Peter the Great.
